statement: The minute hand of a wall clock is $10$ centimeters long. How far, in centimeters, does the tip of the minute hand travel in $20$ minutes?

choices.misconception: I thought the minute hand turns $20^\circ$ in $20$ minutes, so I took $\frac{20}{360}$ of the circumference $20\pi$.
I used $\pi r$ for the circumference instead of $2\pi r$, so I got $\frac{1}{3} \cdot 10\pi$.
I found the area of the sector the hand sweeps, $\frac{1}{3}\pi \cdot 10^2$, instead of the distance the tip travels.

hints: What fraction of a full turn does the minute hand make in $20$ minutes?
The minute hand makes one full turn in $60$ minutes, so in $20$ minutes its tip travels $\frac{20}{60}$ of the circumference $2\pi r$.

solutions.reliable: The tip of the minute hand moves on a circle of radius $10$ cm, whose circumference is $2\pi \cdot 10 = 20\pi$ cm. In $20$ minutes the hand makes $\frac{20}{60} = \frac{1}{3}$ of a turn, so the tip travels $\frac{1}{3} \cdot 20\pi = \frac{20\pi}{3} \approx 20.9$ cm.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
